items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: Wesley Dimes was the bass trumpet man. And, uh, Tim North was the tenor player. And I was Clarence.

ctx.x: Ulyss. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Wesley Dimes was the bass trumpet man. And, uh, Tim North was the tenor player. And I was Clarence. Hmm. Well, what were those guys all from then? They weren't from Rant, Norris? Well, Ulysss was from New Orleans. And, uh, Clarence Thompson, he was from Baton Rouge. Trish was from Baton Rouge.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: And this boy, Wesley Dimes, and the drummer, and myself, we'd make it pretty jumpy at times.

ctx.x: Was Tith Johnson's band, would you call that a pretty ratty band too, or was it mostly?

No, at times it was pretty jumpy. And this boy, Wesley Dimes, and the drummer, and myself, we'd make it pretty jumpy at times. That fellow leading Tith Johnson's band, his name was Oil. I know Lawrence. He was a crippled guy. One leg short another. He was a violin player. Or he could write to. He had Tith Johnson a good band though. Very good band, cause he could write a lot of stuff. He was a fine musician. And he was a violin player. When he could stand up, he'd be drunk all the time. He could, he'd sit in.…
Didn't any of the musicians around here have a drink?
